FAFT: Initialize the TPM handler only on TPM related methods Initializing the TPM handler stops tcsd/trunksd and affects other systems which depend on them. Moving the initializing step to TPM related methods by reusing the LazyInitHandlerProxy class. Also restarted tcsd/trunksd when done. FAFT running on Android system will not run the TPM related tests. So don't care about the Android system. CQ-DEPEND=CL:436245 BUG=chrome-os-partner:62150 TEST=Ran a FAFT test and called the TPM related methods manually. update the snaplen to cover AMSDU aggregation cases While running this test case with AMSDU aggregating wifi card, the test has been failing as the pcap parser was not able to detect the AMSDU subframes from the chopped frame. To detect the UDP stream and the src ip addresses we need to collect the full container. The shanpshot length (snaplen) tcpdump parameter set to 400 was not enough to decode the A-MSDU frame. By spec the aggregated frames in 11n mode can by up to 7935bytes. In case of the NFA344A module, this was around 3560bytes, but lets use the max spec value just in case. BUG=chrome-os-partner:50854 TEST=on Skylake and Apollo Lake platforms with Qualcomm's NFA344A NIC Change-Id: I8036647eb367912c066c951b6e13b6e997f0bdd1 Signed-off-by: Bartosz Markowski <bartosz.markowski@tieto.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/417431 Reviewed-by: Waldemar Rymarkiewicz <waldemar.rymarkiewicz@gmail.com> Reviewed-by: Sameer Nanda <snanda@chromium.org>

elan_i2c: Try to use pid in fw name, with fallback Previously the elan_i2c driver was modified to append a product_id to the end of the filename of the firmware it requests during a firmware update. This caused issues when this version of the driver was used on old systems that had the old no-pid-appended filenames for their firmwares. In an attempt to fix this issue for old systems, the pid was removed from the filename entirely when the driver requests a firmware. Unfortunately, this just breaks firmware updating for any systems with the new with-pid-appended filenames for their firmwares. In this CL we implement the same two-tiered naming convention present in other versions of the elan*_i2c drivers in ChromeOS. First we query to see if there is a valid firmware with a pid appended to the filename. If there is, we use that. However if that file doesn't exist, this patch makes it so the driver will try a fallback filename that does not include the pid. This should work for all systems. BUG=chrome-os-partner:62529 TEST=built kernel and deployed on a kip (new-with-pid-appended) filenames and everything works great. When I manually modify the image to look like an old no-pid-appended system it still works. lakitu: Expand bindmount@.service into .mount units bindmount@.service is a template unit to mimic what a .mount unit does. Unfortunately the RequiresMountsFor directive doesn't take Specifiers as others may do, in the version of systemd we use. This change tries to expand it into individual .mount units instead. The advantage is that the "Default Dependencies" for .mount units should just work - we don't have to craft them by hand. For example systemd automatically adds a Require and After dependency of .mount units for all parent paths so we don't have to do RequiresMountsFor. The downside is that we now need two units to do a bind mount - we used to, too. :) BUG=b:33245793 TEST=trybot Change-Id: Iaa891319751464220bec8e3b3bcfe26ec7d20668 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/435468 Commit-Ready: Daniel Wang <wonderfly@google.com> Tested-by: Daniel Wang <wonderfly@google.com> Reviewed-by: Andrey Ulanov <andreyu@google.com>
